Definition: probably a primary word; flax, i.e. (by implication) "linen":--linen.
BiblicalUsage: línon means flax, linen — a small word with a sharp edge. In Matthew 12:20, "and smoking flax shall he not quench"; and in Revelation 15:6, "clothed in pure and white linen".
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the smoking flax is the bruised reed's twin — Christ will not quench the faintest spark of faith.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
